deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page tabulates log sl φ (sl = sin lemn) and expands log cl φ. This page sets up Gauss's factorisation sl φ = P(φ)/Q(φ), where P is the lemniscatic sigma function and Q its companion. Below, ϖ = 2.62205755 (lemniscate constant) and sl has zeros at ϖ·Z[i].

(1) Coefficients α…θ. These are exactly the Laurent coefficients of 1/sl²φ, which is the Weierstrass ℘ for g2 = 4, g3 = 0, i.e. (y')² = 4y³ − 4y. The identification is my verification, not written on the page:
1/sl²φ = φ^-2 + αφ² + βφ^6 + γφ^10 + δφ^14 + εφ^18 + ζφ^22 + ηφ^26 + θφ^30 + …
The values are α = 1/5, β = 1/75, γ = 2/4875, δ = 1/82875, ε = 2/6215625, ζ = 2/(3³5⁵13²17), η = 4/(3·5⁷13²17·29), θ = 223/(3⁴5⁸13²17²29).
I recomputed all eight from the ℘ recursion c_k = 3/((2k+1)(k−3)) Σ c_m c_{k−m}. Example: for θ the bracket is 31889/(3⁴5⁸13²17²29), and 31889 = 143·223. Gauss records the consecutive ratios α/15, 2β/65, γ/34, 2δ/75, ε/39, 18ζ/725, 223η/9180; all are correct.

(2) Growth of the coefficients. The nearest poles of 1/sl² are ±ϖ and ±iϖ. Hence the ratio of consecutive coefficients tends to ϖ⁴ = 47.268…, which is Gauss's '(2,6220..)⁴ : 1 = 47,27 : 1'.
More precisely, the four double poles give coefficient of φ^(4k−2) ≈ 4(4k−1)/ϖ^(4k) (my derivation). This yields Gauss's 'sehr nahe' values ζ ≈ 92/ϖ²⁴, η ≈ 108/ϖ²⁸, θ ≈ 124/ϖ³², since 92 = 4·23, 108 = 4·27, 124 = 4·31. The relative error is about 1/4096 for ζ; it comes from the next poles at (1±i)ϖ.

(3) log Q. Here Q = P/sl, so (log Q)'' = sl² (my derivation, from −(log P)'' = 1/sl² and (log sl)'' = −1/sl² − sl²). With x = sl φ and d/dφ = √(1−x⁴) d/dx, one gets G'(1−x⁴) − 2x³G = x² for G = d log Q/dx. This forces b_k = (4k−3)/(4k−1)·b_{k−1} with b_1 = 1/3. Hence
log Q = Σ_k [1·5·…(4k−3)]/[3·7·…(4k−1)] · x^(4k)/(4k), as written. It is checked through φ⁸: 1/12·φ⁴ − 1/280·φ⁸.

(4) Bilinear ODE. P P'''' − 4P'P''' + 3P''² = 2P².
This follows from ℘ = −(log P)'' and ℘'' = 6℘² − g2/2 with g2 = 4. The left side equals ½·D⁴(P·P) in Hirota notation, which equals P²(L'''' + 6L''²) with L = log P.

(5) Taylor series of P = σ.
P = φ − 2φ⁵/5! − 36φ⁹/9! + 552φ¹³/13! + 5136φ¹⁷/17! + 5146848φ²¹/21! − …
I checked this by exponentiating log(P/φ) = −Σ c_k φ^(4k)/((4k−1)4k), with c_k = α, β, γ, …. The terms through φ¹⁷ are exact; the φ²¹ term agrees to about 4 significant figures numerically. The reduced fractions (1/(4·3·5), 1/(32·9·5·7), 23/(128·81·25·7·11·13), etc.) are all correct.

(6) Numerical work. Gauss writes P(nϖ) as a series in n with numerical coefficients ϖ, ϖ⁵/60, ϖ⁹/10080, …. These are correct except possibly the last one. At n = 1 the sum is ≈ 0, consistent with σ vanishing at the lattice point ϖ.
At n = ½ the sum is 1.2453446. Gauss identifies this as 2^(−1/4)·1.480974 = 2^(−1/4)·e^(π/8). This is the classical value σ(ω) = e^(ηω/2)·[(e1−e2)(e1−e3)]^(−1/4) with e = 1, 0, −1 and ηω = π/4 for the square lattice.
errors: The coefficient of n^21 in P(nϖ) is written 0,0000620. Using ϖ^21 ≈ 6.18709e8 and 5146848/21! ≈ 1.007394e-13 it should be ≈ 0.0000623. This is a minor slip, or possibly a misreading of the ink.
The exponent 0.3927002 slightly exceeds π/8 = 0.3926991. This is rounding in 1.480974 (true e^(π/8) ≈ 1.480973); harmless.

The last line is labelled 'Pϖ' in the transcription, but P(ϖ) ≈ 0 by the series just above. The value 1.2453446 is P(ϖ/2), obtained by putting n = ½ in the n-series. Either Gauss wrote P½ϖ (faint) or the label is a slip.

If the denominators really read (2ϖ)^24 etc., this conflicts with ϖ = 2.6220575 as used on the same page. The approximations are correct only as 92/ϖ^24, 108/ϖ^28, 124/ϖ^32 with ϖ = 2.622…, so the '2' is probably a misread flourish.

results.what: Laurent coefficients α…θ of 1/sl²φ with exact factorised values and consecutive-ratio relations
results.modern_name: Laurent expansion of the Weierstrass ℘-function for the lemniscatic lattice (g2=4, g3=0), equivalently Eisenstein series G_{4k}(Z[i])
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (℘ recursion, 1850s–1860s lectures); Eisenstein (1847) for lattice sums

results.what: Ratio of successive coefficients tends to ϖ^4 ≈ 47.27, and coefficient of φ^(4k−2) ≈ 4(4k−1)/ϖ^(4k) from the four nearest double poles
results.modern_name: Coefficient asymptotics from nearest singularities (Darboux's method / singularity analysis)

results.what: log Q = Σ [1·5…(4k−3)/(3·7…(4k−1))] x^(4k)/(4k) with x = sl φ, equivalent to (log Q)'' = sl²
results.modern_name: Expansion of the lemniscatic co-sigma/theta quotient in powers of sl (a hypergeometric-type integral of x²/√(1−x⁴))
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Werke III, lemniscatic functions P, Q)

results.what: Bilinear differential equation P P'''' − 4P'P''' + 3P''² = 2P² for the lemniscatic P
results.modern_name: Differential equation of the Weierstrass σ-function (Hirota bilinear form D_x^4 σ·σ = 4σ² for g2 = 4)
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (σ-function, 1882 paper on σ recursions); bilinear formalism Hirota (1971)

results.modern_name: Taylor coefficients of the lemniscatic Weierstrass σ-function
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (general σ); the lemniscatic P is known as Gauss's (Werke III)

results.modern_name: Special value σ(ω₁) = e^(η₁ω₁/2)/((e1−e2)(e1−e3))^(1/4) for the square lattice (Legendre relation gives η₁ω₁ = π/4)
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass/Legendre relation; the lemniscatic value appears in Gauss's notes

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic sigma-type functions P and Q (sl = P/Q), their series, and the value P(ϖ/2) = 2^(−1/4)e^(π/8) are known from his Nachlass (Werke III) and are commonly cited as anticipating Weierstrass. Two details are mildly notable unpublished touches. One is the explicit pole-based coefficient asymptotics 4(4k−1)/ϖ^(4k). The other is the neat bilinear (Hirota-form) ODE for P. Neither is a major priority claim.

checkable.asserts: The α…θ series is the Laurent expansion of ℘ with g2=4, g3=0: (y')²=4y³−4y holds; the result should be O(x**26).
All of Gauss's consecutive-ratio relations hold (should be all True).
The P series satisfies P P'''' − 4P'P''' + 3P''² = 2P² up to the computed order (result O(x**22) if the φ²¹ coefficient is right).
−(log P)'' = 1/sl² (P is the σ-function of the ℘ above); result should be O(x**20).
Gauss's reduced forms of the P coefficients are equal to the factorial forms (should be all True).

transcription_corrections: The last line 'Pϖ = +1,2453446' must denote P(½ϖ), since the n-series gives P(ϖ)≈0 and 1.2453446 results from n = ½. Check the image for a faint '½'.
'(2ϖ)^24', '(2ϖ)^28', '(2ϖ)^32' should almost certainly be read as ϖ^24, ϖ^28, ϖ^32 with ϖ = 2.6220…. Otherwise the approximations are off by a factor 2^24 etc.
In the sentence 'Die Grenze des Verhältnisses zweier aufeinanderfolgender Glieder ist (2,6220..)^4 : 1 = 47,27 : 1', the base is ϖ = 2.6220…
The coefficients α…θ are the Laurent coefficients of 1/sl²φ (φ^-2 + αφ² + βφ^6 + …). They are not directly the log sin lemn table coefficients of the previous page.
The '+' before 'log Q' is probably a marginal mark or sign flourish; the series as written (positive terms) is correct for log Q.
